hero.subtitle: Kennedy Academy is a technology, digital arts and languages academy in El Biar — with a robotics lab, a media studio and a cafe that stay open between sessions.

hub.title: A school that stays open.
hub.intro: Between sessions, the campus becomes a workshop — a robotics lab, a media studio and a cafe where the work continues.

robotics-lab.name: Robotics Lab
robotics-lab.blurb: A hardware bench for prototypes, sensors and competition builds.
robotics-lab.alt: A maker workbench with electronics, tools and a robotics prototype.

media-studio.name: Media Studio
media-studio.blurb: Camera, light and sound — where stories are planned, shot and cut.
media-studio.alt: A camera and lighting setup inside a small media studio.

cafe-coworking.name: Cafe & Coworking
cafe-coworking.blurb: The room between classes: espresso, long tables and unfinished ideas.
cafe-coworking.alt: Warm cafe tables and chairs arranged for coworking.

courses.title: The Course Matrix
courses.intro: Filter by discipline and age, then open a syllabus to see the modules and join the waitlist.

robotics-kids.title: Robotics for Kids
robotics-kids.description: Introductory robotics where children build, wire, and programme their first moving machines through playful, project-based sessions.
robotics-kids.lede: First machines, first circuits, first moment of "we built that".
outcomes: Assemble and wire a working robot from a guided kit.
Explain what a sensor does and use one in a small project.
Debug a simple programme with a mentor's guidance.
Present a finished build to the group.
modules: How machines move — motors, wheels and structure
Circuits and safety — power, switches and sensors
First programme — sequences, loops and timing
Sensor logic — making the robot react
Team build — design, assemble, test
Demo day — present, explain and refine

robotics-juniors.title: Robotics for Juniors
robotics-juniors.description: Advanced robotics for teenagers — sensor integration, team challenges, and competition-ready engineering projects.
robotics-juniors.lede: Engineering with constraints: sensors, competition rules and a team that ships.
outcomes: Design a robot around a defined challenge and rule set.
Integrate multiple sensors and explain the signal flow.
Work in a team with clear build, test and review roles.
Document and pitch an engineering decision.
modules: Challenge brief — constraints, scoring and strategy
Mechanical design — chassis, gearing and torque
Sensor integration — distance, line and touch
Control logic — state machines and calibration
Competition build — iteration under time pressure
Final run — test, present and review

ai-fluency.title: AI Fluency
ai-fluency.description: Age-appropriate AI literacy covering prompts, creative tools, responsible use, and real-world applications students can explain with confidence.
ai-fluency.lede: Understand the tools shaping the next decade — and use them with judgement.
outcomes: Explain how large language models generate and miss information.
Write effective prompts for a defined creative or study task.
Identify bias, hallucination and privacy risks in AI output.
Build a small project that uses AI responsibly.
modules: How AI works — patterns, predictions and limits
Prompt craft — context, constraints and iteration
Creative studio — image, text and sound tools
Responsible use — bias, privacy and attribution
Study and work — AI as a thinking partner
Project clinic — build, critique and present

python-programming.title: Python Programming
python-programming.description: Structured Python foundations from variables and logic to small apps and data projects, taught with patience and practical examples.
python-programming.lede: From first variables to a small application — logic you can carry into any field.
outcomes: Write readable Python using variables, conditionals and loops.
Break a problem into functions and test each piece.
Work with lists, dictionaries and simple files.
Ship a small command-line project.
modules: Variables, types and input
Conditionals and loops
Functions and clean structure
Collections — lists and dictionaries
Files and small data projects
Project week — build, debug and present

languages.title: Languages by Levels
languages.description: French, English, German, and Spanish taught by level — speaking, reading, and conversation practice aligned to each learner's stage.
languages.lede: French, English, German and Spanish — placed by level, taught for real conversation.
outcomes: Speak with more confidence in everyday and classroom situations.
Read and understand level-appropriate texts.
Use grammar with intention rather than memorisation alone.
Prepare for the next level with a clear progress review.
modules: Placement and goals — finding your level
Speaking foundation — rhythm, pronunciation and confidence
Listening and response — real conversations
Reading and vocabulary — building range
Writing and structure — accuracy with purpose
Progress review and next-level plan

audiovisual-training.title: Audiovisual Training
audiovisual-training.description: Film, sound, and visual storytelling — students learn to plan, shoot, and edit content with professional creative discipline.
audiovisual-training.lede: Plan it, shoot it, cut it — visual storytelling with professional discipline.
outcomes: Plan a short film from treatment to shot list.
Operate a camera and capture clean audio.
Edit a sequence with rhythm and continuity.
Screen and critique a finished piece.
modules: Story and treatment — finding the film
Pre-production — shot lists, locations and roles
Camera — framing, movement and exposure
Sound — microphones, levels and room tone
Editing — assembly, rhythm and colour
Screening — critique and final cut

multimedia.title: Multimedia
multimedia.description: Digital design and multimedia production — graphics, layout, and portfolio-ready creative work for the modern creative economy.
multimedia.lede: Design systems, layouts and digital assets that hold up in a real portfolio.
outcomes: Apply layout, type and colour principles to a digital piece.
Build a small multi-page project with a consistent system.
Prepare assets for screen and social formats.
Present a portfolio-ready case study.
modules: Design foundations — grid, type and hierarchy
Colour and image — building a visual system
Layout studio — pages that breathe
Digital production — assets and formats
Portfolio craft — selection and sequencing
Final review — present and refine

method.title: Engineering rigour, open culture.
method.intro: Three commitments shape every programme, every cohort and every room.

rigorous-engineering.title: Rigorous Engineering
rigorous-engineering.body: We teach the reasoning behind the build — structure, constraints, testing, and the discipline to ship something that works.

open-lab-culture.title: Open Lab Culture
open-lab-culture.body: The lab stays open beyond class hours. Students prototype, break things, and learn to ask better questions alongside mentors.

bilingual-fluency.title: Bilingual Fluency
bilingual-fluency.body: Technical English and French are practised inside the work, not bolted on — so students can explain, pitch and collaborate.

testimonials.title: What families say
testimonials.intro: Parents across El Biar and Algiers trust Kennedy School for structured, inspiring education.

sofia.quote: We enrolled in the English and French levels programme. The progression is clear, and our daughter actually looks forward to her sessions every week.
sofia.name: Sofia L.

yasmine.quote: The multimedia course opened a creative path we hadn't considered. Professional atmosphere, warm teachers, and a campus that feels open and modern.
yasmine.name: Yasmine K.
